verdicts.title: Geometric complexity theory and matrix powering
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Valiant's famous determinant versus permanent problem is the flagship problem in algebraic complexity theory. Mulmuley and Sohoni (Siam J Comput 2001, 2008) introduced geometric complexity theory, an approach to study this and related problems via algebraic geometry and representation theory. Their approach works by multiplying the permanent polynomial with a high power of a linear form (a process called padding) and then comparing the orbit closures of the determinant and the padded permanent.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns geometric complexity theory applied to the determinant vs. permanent problem in algebraic complexity, with no mention of resolution proof depth, CNF formulas, or geometric group actions on satisfying assignments. It shares only loose vocabulary ('geometric', 'complexity') with the conjecture.

verdicts.title: The relational complexity of linear groups acting on subspaces
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: The relational complexity of a subgroup $G$ of $\mathrm{Sym}(Ω)$ is a measure of the way in which the orbits of $G$ on $Ω^k$ for various $k$ determine the original action of $G$. Very few precise values of relational complexity are known. This paper determines the exact relational complexity of all groups lying between $\mathrm{PSL}_{n}(\mathbb{F})$ and $\mathrm{PGL}_{n}(\mathbb{F})$, for an arbitrary field $\mathbb{F}$, acting on the set of $1$-dimensional subspaces of $\mathbb{F}^n$. verdicts.title: Survey on Cremona groups from a median geometric point of view
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: This expository article builds on lecture notes from a minicourse entitled "Cremona groups and CAT(0) cube complexes" and given by the author as part of the 2023 Riverside Workshop on Geometric Group Theory. It presents recent constructions of actions of Cremona groups on median graphs aimed at both geometric group theorists and algebraic geometers.
